grammarFocus: 转述动词；引述与改写；限定词 some / most / all 的范围。
title: Media, Information and Evidence: The School Podcast
instructions: 这是一份为B2–C1英语学习者设计的原创听力练习，主题为媒体、信息与证据，重点练习转述动词、引述与改写以及限定词some/most/all的范围。听力材料为一段模拟的学校播客讨论，所有内容均为虚构，用于教学目的。请先听录音（或阅读录音文本），然后回答10个问题。问题类型包括单选、填空、匹配（以单选形式呈现）和判断正误/未提及。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。所有解释均为中文，并附有原文证据。
transcript:
Host: Welcome to The School Podcast. Today we're talking about how we report what we hear. I'm your host, Alex, and with me are two students, Mei and Tom. Mei, you've been looking at how students share news. What did you find?
Mei: Well, I interviewed some students—about twenty—and most of them said they get news from social media. But only a few check the source before sharing. One student told me, 'I just share what my friends post.' That's a common attitude.
Tom: I read a report that claimed all teenagers trust online news. But I think that's an overgeneralization. The report said most teenagers use social media for news, but it didn't say they all trust it. In fact, some students in my class said they doubt what they see.
Host: So you're saying the report exaggerated? Tom: Yes, the writer used 'all' when the evidence only supported 'most'. That's a problem with some media reports—they use strong determiners without enough evidence.
Mei: Exactly. In my interviews, several students mentioned they check the comments to see if others believe the story. But that's not reliable evidence either.
Host: What about the school newspaper? Tom: The school newspaper editor told me they verify facts before publishing. She said, 'We require two sources for every story.' But that's the school paper, not social media.
Mei: Right. So the lesson is: be careful with words like 'all' and 'most'. And when you report what someone said, use verbs like 'claimed', 'stated', or 'admitted' to show your attitude.
Host: Good point. So to summarize, most students get news from social media, some check sources, and not all trust what they see. Thanks for listening.

grammar.title: 转述动词与限定词范围
grammar.explanation: 转述动词如claim, state, admit可以表达说话人的态度；限定词some, most, all表示范围大小，使用时需有证据支持。
grammar.example: The report said most teenagers use social media for news, but it didn't say they all trust it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best reporting verb: The journalist ______ that the event happened, but later admitted it was false.
Which determiner is most accurate if 80% of students own a phone?
She ______ that she had made a mistake. (reporting verb showing willingness to admit)
The survey found that ______ of the participants (about 10%) had read the article.

part1: How do you usually get your news?
Do you check the source before sharing news on social media? Why or why not?
Can you think of a time when you heard a claim that was exaggerated?
What reporting verbs do you know in English?
speaking.part2: Describe a time when you had to check whether information was true. You should say: what the information was, where you heard it, how you checked it, and what the result was.
part3: Why do some media reports use words like 'all' when the evidence only supports 'most'?
How can people be encouraged to verify information before sharing?
What role do reporting verbs play in news reporting?
Do you think social media companies should do more to stop false information? How?

transfer.writing: Write a short paragraph (120-150 words) for a school blog about a time you shared news that turned out to be false. Use at least three different reporting verbs and appropriate determiners (some, most, all). Explain what you learned about checking evidence.
